title: On-prem manifest apply idempotency shim and customer escalation runbook
creator: Avery Chen
description: Summary: Several on-prem tenants reported aborted helm upgrades where the operator reported success but downstream manifests were partially applied (some CRs present, others missing). Investigation shows a race between the operator's reconcile loop and the nodeagent K/V prefix cache leading to a non-idempotent apply path; repeated upgrades sometimes left orphaned CRs and blocked later reconciles. This ticket implements an idempotent manifest-apply shim in the operator and provides a customer-facing escalation runbook for recovery and rollout.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Initial report from SE (ticket #CUST-4829): Upgrade failed during tenant upgrade; customer observed API errors and missing worker CRs.

2026-03-06 - Triage call: reproduced in staging with a scaled concurrency test; operator returned 2xx but manifests were inconsistent across nodes. Suspected non-idempotent apply + cached stale K/V prefixes.

2026-03-08 - Spike completed: added additional telemetry (apply-idempotency, reconcile-episode-id) and confirmation that nodeagent cache TTL correlated with failure rate. Recorded logs and attached to incident doc.

2026-03-10 - Design review: agreed on two-prong approach: 1) conservative idempotent apply shim that computes desired->observed diffs at CR-level and only issues minimal patches; 2) short-term hotfix/rollback playbook for customers to recover without full rollback.
2026-03-12 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/1285 implementing apply-shim and reconcile-episode marker. QA assigned for soak tests.
2026-03-14 - Customer comms: notified three effected customers with mitigation steps; SE provided a scoped runbook for manual remediation if automatic repair is not possible.
2026-03-15 - Current: integration tests green for idempotent shim in k8s 1.27/1.28. Preparing canary rollout to Dedicated infra in next window. On-prem packaging and onprem-helm-chart bump pending.
acceptance_criteria: Operator applies manifests in a way that is safe to retry: repeated re-applies must converge and not create duplicates or orphan CRs.
Automated recovery runbook repairs at least 95% of affected tenants without manual intervention in a staging replay.
Telemetry emits reconcile-episode-id and apply-diff-size metrics; failures trigger alert and link to runbook.
Canary rollout to Dedicated in region us-west-2 with zero data-loss incidents and monitored roll-forward plan.
Customer-facing runbook created and validated with Solutions Engineering for the three flagged customers.
mitigation_steps: 1) If upgrade paused: set operator reconcile to dry-run and record reconcile-episode-id, then run the idempotent repair job: kubectl apply -f repair/repair-manifests-episode-<id>.yaml
2) If operator crashloop: scale operator to 0, clear stuck finalizers on orphaned CRs (kubectl patch) and restart with FEATURE_FLAG_APPLY_SHIM=false for emergency rollback mode,

3) As last resort: snapshot tenant manifests via helm template, perform staged reapply with --wait disabled and validate CR ownership before marking success. Follow customer-specific playbook in Confluence.
4) Notify affected customers via SE playbook with estimated time-to-repair and ask for kubeadmin access if manual remediation is needed.
follow_up_tasks: Backfill end-to-end test covering staggered nodeagent cache resets during concurrent upgrades (ENG test-suite).
Add an operator health endpoint exposing reconcile-episode metrics and last-apply-diff hash.
Evaluate making nodeagent K/V cache TTL adaptive based on upgrade concurrency; spike allocated to R&D (2w).
Documentation: update onprem upgrade troubleshooting guide and internal runbook summarizing lessons learned.
